name: Aegis Authenticator
tagline: Fully offline, open source, encrypted backups — Android only
highlights: Export tokens to an encrypted file at any time — complete, portable, no lock-in
Fully open source, available on F-Droid — no Google Play account required
Encrypted vault with a separate backup password — local storage, no cloud required
verdict: The definitive Android 2FA app. Full control, no third-party dependency, open source. Requires backup discipline.
bestFor: Android users who want maximum control over their 2FA tokens with no cloud dependency and full portability

name: Ente Auth
tagline: Open source, end-to-end encrypted cloud sync, cross-platform — iOS, Android, and desktop
highlights: End-to-end encrypted sync — Ente cannot read your tokens even on their own servers
Cross-platform: Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux, and web app
Shows the next TOTP code before it generates — never wait for a refresh mid-login
verdict: The best cross-platform option with genuine privacy. Open source, E2EE cloud sync, and full export capability. The right choice for iOS users.
bestFor: iOS users, users who want desktop access to their 2FA codes, and anyone who wants cross-platform sync with genuine end-to-end encryption

name: Google Authenticator
tagline: Simple and widely supported — cloud sync added in 2023, but export is a trap
highlights: Google account cloud sync added in May 2023 — but sync reliability has been reported as inconsistent
Export screen places a pre-checked 'Delete all' button next to 'Next' — multiple users report losing all codes
Supported by virtually every site that offers TOTP-based 2FA
verdict: Adequate for casual use, but the export UX is dangerous and cloud sync has reliability issues. Switch to Aegis or Ente Auth.
bestFor: Users who want the simplest possible 2FA app and are primarily on one device — not recommended if you ever plan to switch apps

name: Microsoft Authenticator
tagline: Essential for Microsoft accounts — problematic for everything else
highlights: Passwordless sign-in for Microsoft accounts — the genuine differentiating feature
Circular dependency on new device setup: asks you to authenticate with the app you're trying to set up
Backup reliability issues reported — extended outages with no recovery path for affected users
verdict: Use it for Microsoft accounts if your organization requires it. Keep a separate, more reliable app for non-Microsoft accounts.
bestFor: Work environments mandating Microsoft Authenticator for Microsoft 365 accounts — pair with Aegis or Ente Auth for personal accounts

name: Authy
tagline: Multi-device sync was the selling point — but intentional lock-in and Twilio breach make it a liability
highlights: No token export — by design. Switching to another app requires resetting 2FA on every account manually
Twilio (parent company) suffered a data breach in 2022 that exposed Authy user phone numbers
Blocks GrapheneOS — a more privacy-focused Android variant — from running the app
verdict: Do not recommend for new users. The intentional export lock-in and Twilio breach history are disqualifying. Migrate to Aegis or Ente Auth.
bestFor: Existing users who are already locked in and haven't encountered problems yet — new users should start with Aegis or Ente Auth
